text:
alerts-bot: [ALERT] response-time-slo-warning: p95 > 800ms in us-east-1 for inference-api — paging oncall

sadia g: paging @oncall-sre we're seeing big p95/p99 spikes and streaming stalls across hosted in us-east, lots of customer timeouts :grimacing:

omar r: looking at grafana -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/inference?orgId=1 p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~1.1s in last 3m, p99 ~3.2s. error-rate up from 0.01% -> 0.4%

anya k: streaming stall metric (stream.stall.count) up 4x, batcher queue length for streaming in us-east is 30x baseline, backlog on scheduler hosts

mike l: any deploys in last 30m? I see a canary rollout of runtime-service v2.3.1 started ~10m ago

runtime-eng-bot: deploy detected: runtime-service v2.3.1 canary by reena p at 3509878500 — 3 hosts in canary group

sadia g: @reena p can you confirm whether the kernel-selection optimizer was part of that rollout?

reena p: yes i enabled the new kernel selector flag in the canary (opt-kern=true) to improve long-seq perf. only 3 hosts. will roll back if we see correlation

omar r: traces show a spike in KV cache miss rate and increased syscall latency on canary hosts; scheduler CPU at 95% on the same machines

anya k: streaming sessions are stalling around token ~2k, client-side sees socket stalls and partial payloads. looks like batcher/kv interactions when cache cold

mike l: mitigation ideas: 1) route streaming traffic off canary, 2) temporarily disable continuous-batching, 3) rollback kernel selector canary

reena p: starting rollback now — command: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/runtime-service --to-revision=3509877000` (rolling back canary)

deploy-bot: rollback initiated for runtime-service (rollout id: rtd-3509) — progress: 1/3 nodes updated

oncall-sre: ack, initiating emergency scale for scheduler pool (add +3 replicas) and increasing CPU on affected machines; creating ephemeral autoscaler bump

sadia g: I'm updating status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/3509879999 — marking partial degradation for hosted inference in us-east

omar r: quick check after rollback: p95 down to ~480ms on recovered hosts, p99 still elevated ~2.0s. streaming stalls reduced but not eliminated

anya k: we still see tail spikes on longer sessions — suspect KV cache warming combined with batcher backlog. warm-up may take minutes to stabilize

mike l: short-term config changes: lower `max_batch_size` for streaming routes to 8 and enable prefix cache warmup flag; that should lower batching latency and reduce cold-miss pressure

reena p: applied config to runtime (canary group optics): `max_batch_size=8`, `prefix_cache=true`. watching metrics now

alerts-bot: [PARTIAL RESOLVE] p95 trending downward but p99 remains above SLO — continue monitoring

sadia g: handoff: @oncall-sre take this for the next 60m. I'll capture action items for postmortem: correlate kernel selector change + canary size + KV cache warming + batching config

oncall-sre: ack, taking over. will keep the channel open, escalate to runtime if p99 doesn't drop below 1.5s in next 20m

mike l: customer impact: two enterprise customers reported timeouts, SRE opened support tickets INC-10234 and INC-10235 and notified account teams

reena p: notes for postmortem owners (@omar r @anya k): we should add automated canary health checks for p99 delta, auto-rollback trigger when p99 increases > 2x baseline, and limit kernel selector rollout size until we have cache-warmup gating

sadia g: action items logged: 1) tighten canary thresholds, 2) add p99-delta alert, 3) improve streaming cache warmup, 4) doc runbook for streaming stalls. assigning owners in the incident tracker

oncall-sre: will close live mitigation in 30m if stable. leaving thread open for postmortem updates and timeline additions

sadia g: thanks all — please paste any logs/traces and customer comms here. adding folks to the incident report now. :thumbsup:
